title: HTTP/2 receive-credit batching exceeds the static connection window
fault_primitive: the static-window branch of the vendored HTTP/2 client assigns a connection WINDOW_UPDATE batching threshold of four windows instead of one quarter
incident_class: transport tuning regression causing persistent multiplexed RPC flow-control starvation
symptoms: All application pods remain Running and Ready. Searches initially succeed then time out on the rate RPC, while recommendations, login, and booking paths continue. Search emits sustained downstream request failed / DeadlineExceeded logs; frontend reports failed hotel searches; search rate-attempt and timeout metrics grow despite successful rate-side work.
why_hard: The root cause is on the client side of the named rate dependency, in cumulative HTTP/2 connection credit accounting. Fresh connections briefly pass checks; TCP and Consul remain healthy; completed rate-side spans can mislead responders. A normal default masks the ratio error in the static-window override. Restarts replenish a finite budget, and Deployment rollback keeps the shared ConfigMap contents.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Following search DeadlineExceeded logs into rate capacity, MongoDB, or memcached although rate work completes
Increasing rate QPS capacity or search deadlines without restoring HTTP/2 receive credit
Trusting a successful probe on a newly opened TCP/gRPC connection
Restarting/scaling search and trusting its brief warmup recovery
Rolling back the latest Deployment without reverting the shared source ConfigMap
mitigation_summary: Change the live http2_client.go static-window updateThreshold assignment from uint32(icwz)*4 to uint32(icwz)/4 in search-runtime, then rebuild/restart search. No saved manifests or values are required.

SAYS: The modified gRPC transport waits for a flow-control update threshold four times larger than its receive window. That can stall responses and cause the observed timeouts. I’ve restored search to the original application binary, removing the modified transport, and am checking recovery.

RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deploy/search -- wget -qO- http://localhost:9092/metrics'
SAYS: The rollout is complete. All 60 hotel-search checks returned HTTP 200; the latest checks took 74–199 ms. Search has also completed over 1,800 rate calls with zero timeouts or failures. I’m submitting the mitigation now.
